claim: El Herri, 13 November 1914: Zaian dead numbered 182
whatTheDocumentSays: Not yet consulted directly by this project. The figure is repeated across French-derived reporting and the 1991 HCAR/state monument inscription — see Archival reference.
interpretation: 182 is a French battlefield count, produced by an army that counted its own casualties carefully (pensions and replacements depended on it) but had limited ability or incentive to fully count an enemy in retreat over difficult terrain. It most plausibly functions as a floor, not a total.
counterEvidence: No independent Zaian-side or civilian count exists. The 1991 Moroccan state monument at El Herri repeats the same figure of 182 rather than supplying independent corroboration.
whySourcesDisagree: Not a French-vs-Moroccan dispute in the usual sense — both traditions currently repeat the same uncorroborated number. See Assessments — signed opinions, #3: the monument is not independent corroboration.
archivalReference: ARCHIVAL REFERENCE NOT YET VERIFIED. A researcher would request: SHD Vincennes, GR 3H, Commandement Supérieur (3H 314–752) and the Khénifra Bureau des Affaires Indigènes political bulletins for November 1914.

claim: Annual, July 1921: Spanish dead ranged 7,875 to 13,363
whatTheDocumentSays: Not yet consulted directly. The Expediente Picasso is cited by named scholars in this workspace but has not itself been read at document level.
interpretation: The range is not primarily an evidentiary gap but a definitional one: it moves depending on whether Moroccan troops serving in the Spanish army (Regulares) are counted as Spanish dead.
counterEvidence: No single figure resolves the range. Competing totals cited by different Spanish inquiries and later historians are not corrections of each other — they define the counted population differently.
whySourcesDisagree: Spanish sources are, uniquely, unreliable on their own casualties for this reason. See Source bias and contradictions.
archivalReference: ARCHIVAL REFERENCE NOT YET VERIFIED. A researcher would request the Expediente Picasso original in Spanish military archives.

claim: Casablanca, July–August 1907: bombardment and occupation killed roughly 600 to 3,000+
interpretation: The range is itself evidence of the reporting institutions' incentives: French sources undercount to minimise the scandal of shelling a port city; German sources, for whom embarrassing France served Berlin's interests during the 1905–1911 crisis period, run three to five times higher.
counterEvidence: Moroccan-side figures, where cited at all, run higher still. This workspace has not yet located a Moroccan primary count.
whySourcesDisagree: French 600–1,500; German 2,000–3,000; Moroccan reporting higher still. No party to the event was a disinterested counter.
archivalReference: ARCHIVAL REFERENCE NOT YET VERIFIED. A researcher would request SHD Marine naval and ministerial orders for July 1907, and contemporary press via Gallica (Le Temps, L'Illustration).

claim: Mouha ou Hammou Zayani was killed by his own son Hassan
whatTheDocumentSays: Not applicable — no single document underlies this; it is a recurring claim across secondary literature.
interpretation: This is the most narratively convenient of three competing accounts and the one most often repeated — which is itself grounds for caution, not confidence.
counterEvidence: Two competing accounts exist: death in a clash with a party his own sons had joined, and death at the hands of French-allied partisans. These are not minor variants — they assign responsibility differently.
whySourcesDisagree: Sources emphasising French victory need not resolve which Zayani was fighting whom; sources drawing on family or tribal memory have an interest in either dignifying or explaining away an internal killing. See Assessments — signed opinions, #2.

claim: The August 1953 decision to depose Mohammed V originated in Paris, with Resident-General Guillaume, or with El Glaoui and the notables
interpretation: Three candidate loci of decision are in circulation and this workspace has not established which, because the request that would settle it has not been consulted.
counterEvidence: None yet catalogued — this is an evidentiary gap, not a case of conflicting documents.
whySourcesDisagree: Each tradition tends to place responsibility with the actor least sympathetic to it: French administrative memory emphasises El Glaoui's initiative; Moroccan nationalist memory emphasises French orchestration.
archivalReference: ARCHIVAL REFERENCE NOT YET VERIFIED. A researcher would request the Résidence Générale–Paris correspondence, May–August 1953, Archives diplomatiques de Nantes, Protectorat Maroc.
